text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Italy's bicameral commission set up to carry out constitutional reforms voted in favour of introducing a presidential-style system instead of beefing up the role of the prime minister. The recommendation, approved by 36 votes to 31 with three abstentions, was welcomed by centre-right opposition that had championed a shift to a presidential system (all).

* In an interview, separatist Northern League party leader Umberto Bossi, whose decision to vote in the bicameral commission caused the choice of a presidential system, called the bicameral commission history (Corriere della Sera, La Repubblica).

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said the performance of state accounts over recent months was in line with reaching the target of cutting the country's deficit to three percent of GDP in 1997, fulfilling the key requirement for countries wishing to join the single European currency, the government did not consequently plan any further budgets in 1997. Ciampi also said the country would "certainly" close the current year with an average inflation between 2.1 and 2.2 percent (all).

* A report by national statistics institute Istat showed Italian consumer price inflation rose 1.6 percent year-on-year in May, reaching its lowest level since February 1969, compared with 1.7 percent in April (all).

* In an interview, labour minister Tiziano Treu, whose draft law on reforms to the labour market has just been approved by the chamber of deputies (lower house), said the reforms were inspired by the Dutch model of labour market flexibility (La Repubblica).

* Fund managers association Assogestioni said the inflow into Italy's mutual funds in May was more than 5.7 trillion lire, with share funds gaining over 1.1 trillion lire, against 4.964 trillion in April (Sole 24 Ore).
* Car maker Fiat Auto denied strongly a newspaper report that its Rivalta car plant in Turin was about to be closed (all).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
